items.stem: When is a Conditional Access policy evaluated?

options.rationale: Correct: Conditional Access is enforced after first-factor authentication.
It is not a frontline pre-authentication defense.
It applies broadly, not only at password reset.
It applies to configured users, not only guests.

items.explanation: Correct: Conditional Access is enforced after first-factor authentication.

items.stem: Which TWO are recommended safe-deployment practices for Conditional Access? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Exclude break-glass (emergency access) accounts from policies
options.rationale: Correct: excluding break-glass accounts prevents lockout from misconfiguration.

options.text: Validate new policies in report-only mode first
options.rationale: Correct: report-only lets you see impact before enforcing.

options.text: Enable security defaults alongside Conditional Access
options.rationale: They are mutually exclusive and should not be combined.

options.text: Apply every new policy to all users immediately
options.rationale: Staged rollout with exclusions is safer than a blanket enforce.

items.explanation: Correct: excluding break-glass accounts prevents lockout from misconfiguration.

items.stem: Two policies apply to a user: one requires MFA, another requires a compliant device. What must the user satisfy?

options.text: Both requirements, because assignments and applicable policies combine with AND
options.rationale: Correct: all applicable policies must be satisfied.
Applicable policies are not optional alternatives.
They do not conflict; both apply.
Policy age does not override the requirement to satisfy all applicable policies.

items.explanation: Correct: all applicable policies must be satisfied.
